x-sections.title: General
x-sections.description: The width, indentation, and newlines of all the code.

x-sections.title: Braces and blocks
x-sections.description: Where braces go and the blank lines within blocks and between members.

x-sections.title: Line breaks
x-sections.description: How code that doesn't fit within the line width is split up, and when code is put back on one line.

x-sections.title: Semicolons, commas, and quotes
x-sections.description: The punctuation that's added or removed.

x-sections.title: Spaces
x-sections.description: The spaces around and within parentheses, braces, operators, and keywords.

x-sections.title: Imports and exports
x-sections.description: The sorting, grouping, and line breaks of import and export declarations.

x-sections.title: JSX
x-sections.description: The formatting of JSX elements and attributes.

x-sections.title: Tagged templates
x-sections.description: The formatting of tagged templates and the code embedded in them (ex. `` css`...` ``).

x-sections.title: Ignore comments
x-sections.description: The comments that make the formatter leave code as is.

useTabs.description: Whether to use tabs (true) or spaces (false).

oneOf.description: Uses tabs for indentation.
Uses spaces for indentation.
Always uses semi-colons where applicable.
Prefers semi-colons, but doesn't add one in certain scenarios such as for the last member of a single-line type literal.
Uses automatic semi-colon insertion. Only adds a semi-colon at the start of some expression statements when necessary. Read more: https://standardjs.com/rules.html#semicolons

quoteStyle.description: How to use single or double quotes.

oneOf.description: Always uses double quotes.
Always uses single quotes.
Prefers using double quotes except in scenarios where the string contains more double quotes than single quotes.
Prefers using single quotes except in scenarios where the string contains more single quotes than double quotes.

jsx.quoteStyle.description: How to use single or double quotes in JSX attributes.

oneOf.description: Prefers using double quotes except in scenarios where the string contains more double quotes than single quotes.
Prefers using single quotes except in scenarios where the string contains more single quotes than double quotes.

jsx.sortClassNames.description: How to sort JSX class attribute values, which is either only the kind of sorting or an object with the kind and its options.

oneOf.description: The kind of sorting along with its options.

functions.description: Leading function or tag identifiers whose string arguments and template literals should be sorted as class names (ex. `["cn", "clsx"]`).

attributes.description: Attributes whose values should be sorted as class names in addition to `class` and `className`.

preserveWhitespace.description: Whether to keep the whitespace between class names as is when sorting them.

preserveDuplicates.description: Whether to keep duplicate class names when sorting them.

prefix.description: The prefix the project's Tailwind classes have (ex. `tw` when classes look like `tw:flex`).

theme.description: The theme variables the project adds to Tailwind's default theme and their values, which is what's in `@theme` in its CSS (ex. `{ "--breakpoint-3xl": "120rem", "--color-brand": "#f00" }`).

variants.description: The names of the project's custom variants in the order they're defined, which is what it has an `@custom-variant` for in its CSS.

utilities.description: The names of the project's custom utilities along with the CSS properties each sets, which is what it has an `@utility` for in its CSS (ex. `{ "btn": ["display", "padding"], "tab-*": ["tab-size"] }`).

jsx.sortClassNames.kind.description: How to sort JSX class attribute values.

oneOf.description: Maintains the current class name ordering.
Sorts class names using Tailwind CSS ordering.

quoteProps.description: Change when properties in objects are quoted.

oneOf.description: Remove unnecessary quotes around property names.
Same as 'asNeeded', but if one property requires quotes then quote them all.
Preserve quotes around property names.

jsx.multiLineParens.description: Surrounds the top-most JSX element or fragment in parentheses when it spans multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Never wrap JSX with parentheses and remove existing ones, except when they have comments or are needed (ex. `(<div />).props`).
Prefer wrapping with parentheses in most scenarios, except in function arguments and JSX attributes.
Always wrap JSX with parentheses if it spans multiple lines.

jsx.forceNewLinesSurroundingContent.description: Forces newlines surrounding the content of JSX elements.

oneOf.description: Puts the children of a JSX element on their own lines between its opening and closing tags.
Only puts the children of a JSX element on their own lines when needed, such as when they contain another JSX element.

jsx.bracketPosition.description: If the end angle bracket of a jsx open element or self closing element should be on the same or next line when the attributes span multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Maintains the position of the end angle bracket.
Forces the end angle bracket to be on the same line.
Forces the end angle bracket to be on the next line.

decorators.position.description: Whether a class or class member should be on the same or next line as its decorators.

oneOf.description: Maintains whether it's on the same line as its decorators.
Forces it to be on the same line as its decorators.
Forces it to be on the next line after its decorators.

newLineKind.description: The kind of newline to use.

oneOf.description: For each file, uses the last newline kind found in the file.
Uses carriage return, line feed.
Uses line feed.

useBraces.description: If braces should be used or not.

oneOf.description: Uses braces if they're used. Doesn't use braces if they're not used.
Uses braces when the body is on a different line.
Forces the use of braces. Will add them if they aren't used.
Forces no braces when the header is one line and body is one line. Otherwise forces braces.

bracePosition.description: Where to place the opening brace.

oneOf.description: Maintains the brace being on the next line or the same line.
Forces the brace to be on the same line.
Forces the brace to be on the next line.
Forces the brace to be on the next line if the same line is hanging, but otherwise uses the same line.

singleBodyPosition.description: Where to place the expression of a statement that could possibly be on one line (ex. `if (true) console.log(5);`).

oneOf.description: Maintains the position of the expression.
Forces the whole statement to be on one line.
Forces the expression to be on the next line.

nextControlFlowPosition.description: Where to place the next control flow within a control flow statement.

oneOf.description: Maintains the next control flow being on the next line or the same line.
Forces the next control flow to be on the same line.
Forces the next control flow to be on the next line.

trailingCommas.description: If trailing commas should be used.

oneOf.description: Trailing commas should not be used.
Trailing commas should always be used.
Trailing commas should only be used in multi-line scenarios.

operatorPosition.description: Where to place the operator for expressions that span multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Maintains the operator being on the next line or the same line.
Forces the operator to be on the same line.
Forces the operator to be on the next line.

preferHanging.description: Set to prefer hanging indentation when exceeding the line width instead of making code split up on multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Keeps as much of the code as possible on the current line and continues the rest on the next line with an indent.
Puts each item on its own line.

preferHangingGranular.description: Set to prefer hanging indentation when exceeding the line width instead of making code split up on multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Always prefers hanging regardless of the number of elements.
Only prefers hanging if there is a single item.
Never prefers hanging.

preferSingleLine.description: If code should revert back from being on multiple lines to being on a single line when able. This is very experimental.

oneOf.description: Puts code that spans multiple lines back on a single line when it fits within the line width.
Maintains the code being on multiple lines.

preferSingleLineDefaultTrue.description: If code should revert back from being on multiple lines to being on a single line when able. Defaults to the global `preferSingleLine` value when it's set and otherwise `true`.

oneOf.description: Puts code that spans multiple lines back on a single line when it fits within the line width.
Maintains the code being on multiple lines.

jsxExpressionContainer.preferSingleLine.description: Whether to keep a JSX expression container's braces beside its expression when there's a newline between the open brace and the expression. Only the newline after the open brace is checked, so when this is `false` the close brace goes on its own line even if it was beside the expression. Defaults to the global `preferSingleLine` value when it's set and otherwise `true`.

oneOf.description: Keeps the braces beside the expression even when there's a newline after the open brace. Ex. `{value}`
Puts the braces on their own lines with the expression indented between them when there's a newline after the open brace.

forceSingleLine.description: If code should be forced to be on a single line if able.

oneOf.description: Keeps the code on a single line even when it exceeds the line width, unless it contains a line comment or a comment that spans multiple lines.
Puts the code on multiple lines when it exceeds the line width.

forceMultiLineSpecifiers.description: Whether to force the named imports or exports of a declaration onto multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Puts each specifier on its own line.
Doesn't force the specifiers onto multiple lines.
Puts each specifier on its own line when there's more than one.
Built-in modules (ex. `fs`, `node:path`, `bun:test`, and `cloudflare:workers`).
Imports that aren't built-in or relative, such as packages (ex. `react` and `@scope/pkg`).
Imports from a parent directory (ex. `../utils`).
Imports from the same directory (ex. `./utils`).
Imports of the directory's index (ex. `.` and `./index.js`).
Type-only imports when `module.typeImports` is `"separate"`.
The imports no other group takes. They go in a group at the end when no group lists this.
The imports whose path matches a glob pattern, which take precedence over the categories.

pattern.description: A glob pattern the path of the import is matched against, where `*` doesn't match a `/` (ex. `@/**`).

typeOnlyImportsExportsSortOrder.description: The kind of sort ordering to use for typed imports and exports.

oneOf.description: Puts type-only named imports and exports first.
Puts type-only named imports and exports last.
Does not sort based on if a type-only named import or export, so they're sorted inline with the others.

sortOrder.description: The kind of sort ordering to use.

oneOf.description: Maintains the current ordering.
Alphabetically and case sensitive.
Alphabetically and case insensitive.

deno.description: Top level configuration that sets the configuration to what is used in Deno.

oneOf.description: Uses the configuration Deno uses.
Uses the configuration of this plugin.

arrowFunction.useParentheses.description: Whether to use parentheses around a single parameter in an arrow function.

oneOf.description: Forces parentheses.
Maintains the current state of the parentheses.
Prefers not using parentheses when possible.

binaryExpression.linePerExpression.description: Whether to force a line per expression when spanning multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Formats with each part on a new line.
Maintains the line breaks as written by the programmer.

conditionalExpression.linePerExpression.description: Whether to force a line per expression when spanning multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Formats with each part on a new line.
Maintains the line breaks as written by the programmer.

conditionalType.linePerExpression.description: Whether to force a line per expression when spanning multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Formats with each part on a new line.
Maintains the line breaks as written by the programmer.

conditionalExpression.indentBranchConten.description: Whether to indent the hanging content of a conditional expression's true or false part past the start of that part when its `?` or `:` starts the line (ex. the properties of `? {` are indented past the `{` instead of lined up with it). This has no effect when the indent width is greater than 2 because the content is already past the start of the part.

oneOf.description: Indents the hanging content past the start of the part (ex. `? {` then `    prop: 1,` then `  }` at an indent width of 2).
Indents the hanging content once from the start of the line, so it lines up with the start of the part when the indent width is 2.

useNestedIndentation.description: Whether to indent a nested conditional in the true or false part more than its parent, so it formats as a tree.

oneOf.description: Indents nested conditionals.
Keeps the false part of a nested conditional at the same indentation as its parent.

memberExpression.linePerExpression.description: Whether to force a line per expression when spanning multiple lines.

oneOf.description: Formats with each part on a new line.
Maintains the line breaks as written by the programmer.

taggedTemplate.formatEmbedded.description: Whether to format the text of tagged templates whose tag is in `taggedTemplate.embeddedLanguages` (ex. `` html`...` `` and `` css`...` ``) with the plugin dprint uses for the language's file extension. A template is left as is when no plugin formats the extension.

oneOf.description: Formats the text of the tagged templates in `taggedTemplate.embeddedLanguages`.
Leaves the text of tagged templates as is.

taggedTemplate.embeddedLanguages.description: Map of a tagged template's tag to the file extension of the language its text is formatted as, which replaces the defaults. The styled-components patterns (ex. `` styled.div`...` `` and `` styled(Button)`...` ``) use the `css` entry. The text of css is formatted as Less by default because the placeholders of its expressions are Less variables.

memberSpacing.description: How to space the members of a class, enum, interface, or type literal.

oneOf.description: Forces a new line between members.
Forces a blank line between members.
Maintains whether a newline or blankline is used.

blockPadding.description: Whether to keep blank lines at the start and end of a block.

oneOf.description: Removes the blank lines at the start and end of a block.
Maintains the blank lines at the start and end of a block.
Forces a blank line at the start and end of a block that isn't empty.

typeLiteral.separatorKind.description: The kind of separator to use in type literals.

oneOf.description: Use semi-colons.
Use semi-colons. Same as "semicolon".
Use commas.

spaceAround.description: Whether to place spaces around enclosed expressions.

oneOf.description: Ex. `myFunction( true )`
Ex. `myFunction(true)`

spaceAfterControlFlowKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the keyword of a control flow statement and before its open paren. This is the default for the `spaceAfter...Keyword` options of the `if`, `for`, `for...in`, `for...of`, `while`, `do...while`, `with` and `switch` statements and the catch clause.

oneOf.description: Ex. `if (true)`
Ex. `if(true)`

spaceSurroundingProperties.description: Whether to add a space surrounding the properties of single line object-like nodes.

oneOf.description: Ex. `{ key: value }`
Ex. `{key: value}`

mappedType.spaceSurroundingProperties.description: Whether to add a space surrounding the properties of a single line mapped type.

oneOf.description: Ex. `type Test = { [key in Type]: string }`
Ex. `type Test = {[key in Type]: string}`

objectExpression.spaceSurroundingPropert.description: Whether to add a space surrounding the properties of a single line object expression.

oneOf.description: Ex. `{ key: value }`
Ex. `{key: value}`

objectPattern.spaceSurroundingProperties.description: Whether to add a space surrounding the properties of a single line object pattern.

oneOf.description: Ex. `{ key: value } = obj`
Ex. `{key: value} = obj`

typeLiteral.spaceSurroundingProperties.description: Whether to add a space surrounding the properties of a single line type literal.

oneOf.description: Ex. `type Test = { key: string }`
Ex. `type Test = {key: string}`

spaceBetweenObjectClosingBraces.description: Whether to keep a space between the closing braces of a nested object and its parent in single-line objects, destructuring patterns, and type literals.

oneOf.description: Ex. `const { key: { value } } = obj;`
Ex. `const { key: { value }} = obj;`

binaryExpression.spaceSurroundingBitwise.description: Whether to surround the operator in a binary expression with spaces.

catchClause.spaceAfterCatchKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `catch` keyword in a catch clause.

oneOf.description: Ex. `catch (err)`
Ex. `catch(err)`

commentLine.forceSpaceAfterSlashes.description: Forces a space after the double slash in a comment line.

oneOf.description: Ex. `//test` -> `// test`
Ex. `//test` -> `//test`

constructor.spaceBeforeParentheses.description: Whether to add a space before the parentheses of a constructor.

oneOf.description: Ex. `constructor ()`
Ex. `constructor()`

constructorType.spaceAfterNewKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `new` keyword in a constructor type.

oneOf.description: Ex. `type MyClassCtor = new () => MyClass;`
Ex. `type MyClassCtor = new() => MyClass;`

constructSignature.spaceAfterNewKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `new` keyword in a construct signature.

oneOf.description: Ex. `new (): MyClass;`
Ex. `new(): MyClass;`

doWhileStatement.spaceAfterWhileKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `while` keyword in a do while statement.

oneOf.description: Ex. `} while (condition);`
Ex. `} while(condition);`

exportDeclaration.spaceSurroundingNamedE.description: Whether to add spaces around named exports in an export declaration.

oneOf.description: Ex. `export { SomeExport, OtherExport };`
Ex. `export {SomeExport, OtherExport};`

forInStatement.spaceAfterForKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `for` keyword in a "for in" statement.

oneOf.description: Ex. `for (const prop in obj)`
Ex. `for(const prop in obj)`

forOfStatement.spaceAfterForKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `for` keyword, or the `await` keyword in a `for await`, in a "for of" statement.

oneOf.description: Ex. `for (const value of myArray)` or `for await (const value of myArray)`
Ex. `for(const value of myArray)` or `for await(const value of myArray)`

forStatement.spaceAfterForKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `for` keyword in a "for" statement.

oneOf.description: Ex. `for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++)`
Ex. `for(let i = 0; i < 5; i++)`

forStatement.spaceAfterSemicolons.description: Whether to add a space after the semi-colons in a "for" statement.

oneOf.description: Ex. `for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++)`
Ex. `for (let i = 0;i < 5;i++)`

functionDeclaration.spaceBeforeParenthes.description: Whether to add a space before the parentheses of a function declaration.

oneOf.description: Ex. `function myFunction ()`
Ex. `function myFunction()`

functionExpression.spaceBeforeParenthese.description: Whether to add a space before the parentheses of a function expression.

oneOf.description: Ex. `function<T> ()`
Ex. `function<T>()`

functionExpression.spaceAfterFunctionKey.description: Whether to add a space after the function keyword of a function expression.

oneOf.description: Ex. `function <T>()`
Ex. `function<T>()`

functionExpression.flatIife.description: Whether to skip indenting the body of a function expression used in an IIFE.

oneOf.description: Does not indent the body of the function in `(function() { ... })();`.
Indents the body as normal.

getAccessor.spaceBeforeParentheses.description: Whether to add a space before the parentheses of a get accessor.

oneOf.description: Ex. `get myProp ()`
Ex. `get myProp()`

ifStatement.spaceAfterIfKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `if` keyword in an "if" statement.

oneOf.description: Ex. `if (true)`
Ex. `if(true)`

importDeclaration.spaceSurroundingNamedI.description: Whether to add spaces around named imports in an import declaration.

oneOf.description: Ex. `import { SomeExport, OtherExport } from "my-module";`
Ex. `import {SomeExport, OtherExport} from "my-module";`

jsxSelfClosingElement.spaceBeforeSlash.description: Whether to add a space before a JSX element's slash when self closing.

oneOf.description: Ex. `<Test />`
Ex. `<Test/>`

jsxExpressionContainer.spaceSurroundingE.description: Whether to add a space surrounding the expression of a JSX container. An object or array literal uses `jsxExpressionContainer.spaceSurroundingObjectLiteral` or `jsxExpressionContainer.spaceSurroundingArrayLiteral`, which default to this value.

oneOf.description: Ex. `{ myValue }`
Ex. `{myValue}`

jsxExpressionContainer.spaceSurroundingO.description: Whether to add a space between the braces of a JSX container and an object literal. Parens that get removed are looked through (ex. `{({ value: true })}`), but a literal with a comment beside it uses `jsxExpressionContainer.spaceSurroundingExpression`.

oneOf.description: Ex. `{ { value: true } }`
Ex. `{{ value: true }}`

jsxExpressionContainer.spaceSurroundingA.description: Whether to add a space between the braces of a JSX container and an array literal. Parens that get removed are looked through (ex. `{([value])}`), but a literal with a comment beside it uses `jsxExpressionContainer.spaceSurroundingExpression`.

oneOf.description: Ex. `{ [value] }`
Ex. `{[value]}`

method.spaceBeforeParentheses.description: Whether to add a space before the parentheses of a method.

oneOf.description: Ex. `myMethod ()`
Ex. `myMethod()`

setAccessor.spaceBeforeParentheses.description: Whether to add a space before the parentheses of a set accessor.

oneOf.description: Ex. `set myProp (value: string)`
Ex. `set myProp(value: string)`

switchStatement.spaceAfterSwitchKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `switch` keyword in a switch statement.

oneOf.description: Ex. `switch (value)`
Ex. `switch(value)`

taggedTemplate.spaceBeforeLiteral.description: Whether to add a space before the literal in a tagged template.

oneOf.description: Ex. `` html `<element />` ``
Ex. `` html`<element />` ``

typeAnnotation.spaceBeforeColon.description: Whether to add a space before the colon of a type annotation.

oneOf.description: Ex. `function myFunction() : string`
Ex. `function myFunction(): string`

typeAssertion.spaceBeforeExpression.description: Whether to add a space before the expression in a type assertion.

oneOf.description: Ex. `<string> myValue`
Ex. `<string>myValue`

whileStatement.spaceAfterWhileKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `while` keyword in a while statement.

oneOf.description: Ex. `while (true)`
Ex. `while(true)`

withStatement.spaceAfterWithKeyword.description: Whether to add a space after the `with` keyword in a with statement.

oneOf.description: Ex. `with (obj)`
Ex. `with(obj)`

lineWidth.description: The width of a line the printer will try to stay under. Note that the printer may exceed this width in certain cases.

indentWidth.description: The number of columns for an indent.

maxBlankLines.description: The maximum number of consecutive blank lines to keep.

module.blankLinesAfterImports.description: The number of blank lines to force after the import declarations at the top of a module. When not set, maintains the blank lines up to `maxBlankLines`.

module.importGroups.description: Ordered list of import groups, separated by blank lines. Empty disables the feature. A group's patterns take the imports they match wherever the group is listed, the categories take the rest, and the list sets the output order.

match.description: The imports in the group, as a category, a pattern, or a list of them.

oneOf.description: A list of categories and patterns whose imports go in the same group.

module.typeImports.description: How `module.importGroups` classifies type-only imports (ex. `import type { Foo } from "./foo";`).

oneOf.description: Classifies type-only imports as the `type` category, so they can be put in their own group.
Classifies type-only imports by their path like the other imports.

module.importGroupsNewlinesBetween.description: How to put blank lines between the imports when `module.importGroups` is set. Mirrors the `newlines-between` option of ESLint's `import/order` rule.

oneOf.description: Puts one blank line between groups and removes the blank lines within a group.
Puts one blank line between groups and keeps the blank lines within a group.
Removes the blank lines between all the imports.
Neither adds nor removes blank lines.

ignoreNodeCommentText.description: The text to use for an ignore comment (ex. `// dprint-ignore`).

ignoreFileCommentText.description: The text to use for a file ignore comment (ex. `// dprint-ignore-file`).
